title: A few founders leave
hook: Track a small population through one event.

knows: An allele is a variant of a gene.
doesNotKnow: A small founder group can have a different allele frequency from the source population by chance. Its later evolution depends on further events.

misconception: Population size and allele frequency always change together.
objective: Count allele frequency in a finite haploid population after a specified event.

claims.text: Question, stage and explanation: In a haploid model, each dot is one individual with one A or a allele. Start with 6 A and 4 a. Exactly 1 A and 3 a individuals found a new isolated population. What fraction of the resulting group carries A? The resulting group has 1 A and 3 a, so its A frequency is 1 out of 4. A small founder group can have a different allele frequency from the source population by chance. Its later evolution depends on further events. The diagram fixes this one outcome rather than predicting every real population.
claims.source: Specified finite population; biological context: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/19-1-population-evolution

claims.text: Each dot stands for one haploid individual with one allele at this locus; colours do not imply actual organism colours.
Recall: If a haploid group has 1 A individuals and 3 a individuals, what fraction carry A? There are 4 individuals and 1 carry A.
claims.source: Finite count defined by the question.

recall.question: If a haploid group has 1 A individuals and 3 a individuals, what fraction carry A?
recall.why: There are 4 individuals and 1 carry A.
